newsitem.title: JAPAN: S'tomo Bank sinks on appeal filing.
newsitem.headline: S'tomo Bank sinks on appeal filing.

text.p: Sumitomo Bank Ltd shares sank on Wednesday morning, still depressed by news that two employees at its California subsidiary had filed an appeal with the U.S. Federal Deposit Insurance Corp claiming that the unit's loan policies ran afoul of U.S. regulations.
As of 0106 GMT, the shares were down 50 yen at 1,720, on turnover of about 2.4 million shares, the second-most heavily traded issue on the first section of the Tokyo bourse.

Sumitomo said in a statement on Tuesday that it had been informed by a subsidiary, Sumitomo Bank of California, that two employees of the unit had filed an appeal with the Federal Deposit Insurance Corp (FDIC).
"It is not true that the FDIC has launched a probe of the American unit over the issue, and the unit has been managed under U.S. regulations," Sumitomo said the statement.

Earlier on Tuesday, Kyodo News Agency reported that two loan examiners filed suit against the Sumitomo unit in California for compensation for losses they say they suffered after refusing to go along with the bank's senior managers in extending loans.
Kyodo said the plaintiffs issued a statement saying they had already asked the FDIC to investigate the bank's loan policies.
